subject: OrbitAI technical next-steps: SLOs, topology & PoC agenda
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitai.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@orbitai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T13:02:00Z
Subject: OrbitAI technical next-steps: SLOs, topology & PoC agenda

Thanks again for the productive call this morning — appreciated the clear framing. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single reference.

Problem / priority summary (from the call)
- Real-time classification workflows with occasional bulk reprocessing.
- Tight p95 latency requirement for immediate API responses: targeting <=120ms for single-turn requests at median payloads (~256 tokens).
- Throughput: baseline 200 QPS during business hours; bursts to ~600 QPS for scheduled peaks.
- Multi-tenant isolation: each customer requires per-tenant routing and auditability (no shared KV caches between tenants).

Model / infra constraints you mentioned
- Multi-turn chat for some flows (small KV cache per session).
- Prefer a 13B–70B open model family; you called out wanting to try a 70B quantized variant for quality comparisons.
- Dataset contains PII; SOC2 + encryption-at-rest are blockers for any hosted trial beyond a sandbox.

Proposed topology for PoC (attached: orbitai_topology.png)
- Hosted PoC on Redwood Dedicated with a VPC peering option for secure traffic.
- Route inference by latency class: latency-sensitive traffic to a low-latency cluster (smaller context, aggressive batching disabled), batch jobs to a separate autoscaled pool with larger sequence lengths and quantized models.
- Per-tenant routing layer + prefix-based KV cache disabled across tenants; cache scoped to tenant_id.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Liam: confirm the 120ms p95 target for the narrow real-time endpoints (yes/no).
2) OrbitAI to share a small sample of average request payload (tokens) and tokenization corner cases by EOD Friday — we'll use this to pick kernel paths and batching configs.
3) Redwood to share: (a) a proposed PoC agenda and timeline, (b) an initial ops runbook for canarying, and (c) an estimated cost envelope for Dedicated pilot.

Attachments: orbitai_topology.png (diagram), redwood_poc-timeline.xlsx (PoC schedule draft), redwood_mpa_draft.pdf (mutual action plan draft)

Thanks — I’ll pick up scheduling the next technical deep-dive after we get the payload samples.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_poc-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@orbitai.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: OrbitAI technical next-steps: SLOs, topology & PoC agenda

Thanks Priya — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: 120ms p95 is our target for the customer-facing real-time endpoints (this is strict for the top 10 customers). For other customers ~200–250ms is tolerable.
- Payloads: average request ~140 tokens, 95th percentile ~320 tokens. We do have some long-context jobs (~2k tokens) run as batch; those can be routed to the batch pool.
- Model: we want to start with a quantized 33B variant (quality/cost sweet spot) and then test a 70B for a subset of flows where quality delta matters. Quantization to 4-bit is preferred if you support it with stable kernels.

Security: we can start with a pseudonymized sandbox dataset for functional PoC. For anything beyond that we’ll need SOC2 evidence and KMS integration.

Action items from our side:
- Sofia will drop a small sample payload set (csv + sample tokens) and a short doc describing our tenant isolation requirements by EOD Thursday.
- I’ll confirm our preferred weeks for the 2-week PoC window (tentatively Aug 2–13).

One technical question: how does Redwood handle prefix caching and KV cache busts for multi-turn state when you’re doing per-tenant isolation? We need to ensure session stitching works across our autoscaling policy.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Product, OrbitAI
[Attachment: orbitai_sample_payloads.csv (csv)]

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@orbitai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@orbitai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Looping in some procurement context so we can avoid surprises later. A couple of notes: 
- Contracting: we usually need a standard SaaS SOW + SOC2 annex to proceed; please include a draft SOW in the MPA if possible.
- Billing: monthly invoicing ok for the pilot; we may ask for a one-time onboarding credit depending on cost envelope.

Schedules: Aug 2–13 works for a PoC slot. We’d like a half-day deep-dive (engineering + infra) on week one and then a short validation window in week two.

Thanks — sending sample payloads now (attached).

Best,
Sofia Martinez
VP, Platform & Ops, OrbitAI

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: OrbitAI technical next-steps: SLOs, topology & PoC agenda

Internal note — forwarding the thread and attachments from OrbitAI. Highlights + ask for ENG/Infra review: 

1) Latency profile: p95 <= 120ms for top customers; median payload ~140 tokens, p95 ~320 tokens. Burst to 600 QPS.
2) Model plan: start with 33B quantized (4-bit preferred), optionally test 70B for quality lift.
3) Isolation: strict per-tenant KV cache; do not allow cross-tenant prefix reuse. Need an ops-safe approach to session stitching under autoscale.

Primary asks for Karthik / infra team:
- Quick feasibility check on 33B 4-bit kernel stability for our target GPUs and the expected p95 at 200 QPS with tenant-scoped caches.
- Draft an ops canary for canarying model variant rollouts (include rollback time targets).
- Rough cost estimate for a 2-week Dedicated PoC with the topology in orbitai_topology.png.

I’ve attached the PoC timeline and MPA draft for your edits. Can you take an initial pass today so I can share a cleaned version back to OrbitAI by EOD?

Thanks — Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_mpa_draft.pdf (pdf)]
